title: Benny Rides Again, Clarinet a la King and Superman
summary: His feelings about the major Goodman pieces: nostalgia, doing what he could.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I'd like to talk for a few minutes about I guess what I consider and what a lot of other people consider, the most important things you did for Benny, things like 'Benny Rides Again' and 'Clarinet a la King' and 'Superman' and works like that. What do you think about those?
I really don't know. When I listen to those things, for me

it's like picking up a photograph, it brings back--it's always a nostalgic enterprise for me--it brings back smells, much better than a photograph. It's a whole sense of what it is like to be around then. That's how I see it, I don't see it in any other terms.
So that doesn't help you very much.
Did you feel that you were doing something particularly ambitious when you were writing those, because they sound very ambitious?

No, I think that whenever I've done anything it's what I could do at that moment. I don't like to pander, because I feel that everytime you do something--I like to do something that stretches, that pushes the limit, because if you don't, you fall back into that sort of pattern that we were discussing before. Ambitious is not the term I would use; it's what I could do and what
concerned me most of the time was that sort of thi g. I did it in the form it was, because that's who I was doing it for. If there was another situation it wouldn't have been that at all.
